question: What is the volume in milliliters of a system comprised of 0.312 kg Freon-12 refrigerant when placed at the bottom of the Marianas Trench and allowed to stabilize at the Trench's peak temperature, rounded to the nearest mL? Provide your answer as just an integer value.

history.name: Thermodynamics_Expert

Then we will determine the phase of Freon-12 at those conditions, select an appropriate property model (likely liquid with a pressure-dependent density via Tait equation or compressibility), compute the volume from mass/density, convert to milliliters, and round to the nearest integer. DeepSeaData_Expert, please provide the peak bottom temperature and pressure.

history.content: Peak bottom temperature near Challenger Deep has been reported around 4°C. Pressure at ~10,900–11,000 m depth is approximately 1,090 bar (≈109 MPa, about 1,076–1,080 atm). These are representative peak conditions; I recommend we use 4.0–4.1°C and 1,090 bar for calculations.

Baseline liquid density near 0–5°C at ~1 atm is about 1.49 g/mL. Using liquid compressibility/Tait-type behavior, density should increase modestly under 109 MPa, likely toward 1.6–1.7 g/mL. I will perform a Tait-style estimate next.

That yields roughly ρ ≈ 1.66 g/mL. With mass 312 g, Volume ≈ 312/1.66 ≈ 188 mL. We can refine, but this is a reasonable ballpark.
